newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices soften on milder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices soften on milder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices erased previous gains on Thursday, ladened by mild weather forecasts in the eastern U.S. and significant weakness in the futures market, industry sources said.

Gulf Coast prices fell by about 10 cents to the high-$2.40s to low-$2.50s as above-normal temperatures in the Northeast and moderating weather in the producing region dissuaded buyers from entering the market.
At the Henry Hub, La., most deals were confirmed done around the $2.50 area, but some late shortcovering resulted in limited deals as high as $2.59.
Henry Hub November natgas futures, which expire Friday, reached a low of $2.46 in Thursday's session, down 11.5 cents from Wednesday's settlement.
In Texas, a return to more seasonable weather pressured prices on those pipes into the low-to-mid $2.40s, down about 10 cents on the day.
In the Midcontinent, the lack of buying interest also pushed prices about 10 cents lower into the low-to-mid $2.30s.
The Chicago city-gate market continued its late Wednesday retreat, trading mostly in the low-$2.70s, as compared to the $2.80-2.85 range seen on Wednesday.
Similarly in west Texas, Permian prices fell more than 10 cents to the high-$2.20s to mid-$2.30s as demand to the west eased.
At the southern California border, Day 1 gas sold in the high-$2.40s, falling more than five cents from Wednesday's level.
On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices slumped into the $2.80s early and then into the $2.70s late as some buyers reportedly turned back volumes of gas purchased earlier in the week.
